name: Rosewood Baha Mar
positioning: Resort in Nassau, The Bahamas, with rooms, suites and oceanside villas, Mexican and French restaurants and a Jack Nicklaus-designed golf course
best_for: Families or groups who want multi-room suites with multiple bedrooms or connecting options
Travelers who want golf, snorkeling and food-focused experiences in The Bahamas

facts.text: Rosewood Baha Mar is in Nassau, The Bahamas.
Costa serves coastal flavors with creative Mexican flair, aimed at those who love fresh seafood.
Café Boulud The Bahamas serves traditional French cuisine in a Bahamian setting.
Manor Bar serves classic handcrafted cocktails.
The Library serves champagne, Bahamian bush teas and bites.
Breakfast Café is an outdoor breakfast venue.
Light meals and drinks are served at the pool and beach by the water's edge.
Costa hosts a Sunday Mexican brunch crafted by Chef Juan Meza.
Every Tuesday and Saturday, bartenders at Costa run a margarita-making class.
Every Thursday afternoon Café Boulud offers Kristal Caviar with a selection of martinis.
Multi-room suites with multiple bedrooms or connecting options suit families or groups.
The oceanside villas have living spaces and residential amenities.

highlights.text: Flamingo Yoga is a yoga class shared with flamingos.
The Ocean Guardian Experience is a guided snorkel through reefs and underwater sculptures.
The Royal Blue Golf Course was designed by Jack Nicklaus and is an 18-hole, par-72 course.
Hussey's Art Tour is a guided tour of local art and artists with a creative workshop and conversation over champagne.
Tingum on the Sand is a toes-in-the-sand dining experience.

considerations.text: Tingum on the Sand takes no reservations; seating is first come, first served.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the ultra-luxury positioning.
WhataHotel notes the large resort complex may feel overwhelming for those seeking an intimate getaway.
